objective: Signed numbers describe direction from zero
constraints: real-world contexts (temperature, elevation, money); values from -20 to 20
hints: Decide whether the statement gives a position relative to a zero level or a change from a stated starting level.
For a position, use above/below the reference; for a change, use increase/decrease from the start.
Keep the stated distance unchanged and attach the direction sign that matches the situation.

objective: Locate integers on the number line
constraints: integers from -10 to 10; moves start at 0
hints: Start at the stated zero point on the number line.
Move the stated number of unit intervals in each direction, continuing from each previous landing point.
Read the signed coordinate of the final point.

constraints: integers from -20 to 20; include 0 occasionally
hints: Which value is equally far from zero on the other side?
Reverse the sign once for each stated opposite.
Remember that zero is its own opposite and check the reversals.

constraints: up to three nested opposites; integers from -12 to 12
hints: Which value is equally far from zero on the other side?
Reverse the sign once for each stated opposite.
Remember that zero is its own opposite and check the reversals.

constraints: integers from -10 to 10
hints: Place every supplied value on one number line, with larger values farther right.
For an ordering request, list every input once from left to right; for a single comparison, identify only the requested extreme.
Check the selected value lies on the required side of each compared value.

constraints: integers from -10 to 10
hints: Locate both integer endpoints on a number line.
Count the unit gaps between them, splitting at zero when endpoints lie on opposite sides.
Report that nonnegative gap count, not the number of labelled points.

constraints: integers from -12 to 12; include negative-negative pairs
hints: Locate both values and identify which position is smaller.
Aim the narrow point of the comparison mark toward that smaller position.
Read the completed relation aloud from left to right to confirm it states the true ordering.

constraints: true/false judgments and chains of up to three integers
hints: First identify whether the prompt asks for a truth judgment, an ordered chain, or both.
Test a displayed relation on the number line; for a chain, sort every supplied value from left to right.
Return only the requested part, checking adjacent relations when an ordered chain is required.

constraints: integers from -20 to 20
hints: Absolute value asks for distance from zero, not signed location.
Evaluate any inside expression first, then take its nonnegative distance.
Check that an absolute value cannot be negative.

constraints: sum or difference of two absolute values
hints: Evaluate each absolute-value term separately as its nonnegative distance from zero.
Keep the original plus or minus operation between those two evaluated values.
Distinguish a nonnegative bar value from a whole subtraction expression that can be negative.

objective: Adding integers with the same sign
constraints: integers from -12 to 12; both addends negative or both positive
hints: Identify that both addends have the same sign.
Add their absolute values to find the total distance from zero.
Keep the shared sign and check magnitude is the sum of both distances.

constraints: integers from -12 to 12; one positive, one negative addend
hints: Compare the absolute values of the two addends.
Subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger magnitude.
Keep the sign of the addend with larger magnitude; equal opposite magnitudes finish at zero.

constraints: sums that cancel to 0; up to three addends from -12 to 12
hints: Group contributions that move right and contributions that move left.
Compare the total distance in each direction; equal totals cancel at the starting point.
When one total is larger, use that direction and the difference of the two distances for the final location.

objective: Rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite
constraints: integers from -12 to 12; subtrahend positive
hints: Keep the first integer unchanged.
Replace subtraction of the positive second integer with addition of its negative opposite.
Apply signed addition and check the result lies left of the starting value.

constraints: integers from -12 to 12; subtrahend negative
hints: Rewrite subtraction as addition of the opposite of the second number.
Reverse the subtrahend sign, then apply integer addition.
Check that subtracting a negative becomes adding its positive opposite.

constraints: integers from -12 to 12; mix all four sign cases
hints: Rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite of the second value.
For matching signs, add the magnitudes and keep their shared sign. For opposite signs, subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger.
For opposite signs, keep the sign of the larger-magnitude addend. Equal opposites cancel to zero; check the result against the original operation.

objective: Chains of three or more terms
constraints: three or four terms; integers from -15 to 15
hints: Rewrite every subtraction as addition of an opposite.
Keep every sign attached and combine opposite pairs or use a running total.
Check every original term occurs once and regroup differently to verify.

constraints: one missing term; integers from -12 to 12
hints: Identify whether the blank is an addend, starting value, or amount removed.
Use: addend = sum minus known addend; start = result plus removed amount; removed amount = start minus result.
Substitute the found value into the unchanged signed equation to verify it.

constraints: factors from -12 to 12; exactly one negative factor
hints: Check first whether either factor is zero.
Otherwise multiply the magnitudes and use the effect of one factor below zero on the product direction.
Check by repeated addition using the positive factor as the number of equal groups.

constraints: factors from -12 to 12; both factors negative
hints: Count whether there are zero, one, or two negative factors or values.
An odd count of negatives gives negative; an even count gives positive.
Compute the magnitude with whole-number facts and attach that sign.

constraints: divides evenly; values from -60 to 60; exactly one negative
hints: Identify dividend and nonzero divisor, including the zero-dividend case.
Divide absolute values in original order and determine quotient sign from the two operands.
Multiply the candidate quotient by the divisor to recover the dividend.

constraints: divides evenly; values from -60 to 60; both negative
hints: Count whether there are zero, one, or two negative factors or values.
An odd count of negatives gives negative; an even count gives positive.
Compute the magnitude with whole-number facts and attach that sign.
